suggestions.assertion: At most one full TDD workflow drove the change: superpowers:test-driven-development or Matt Pocock's tdd, not both as drivers (objective: single_tdd_driver...)
suggestions.reason: In this without_skill run, no skill of any kind was invoked, so this check passes vacuously -- it cannot fail when zero skills are used. It is only discriminating in combo/mp-style conditions where a driver conflict is actually possible. Worth flagging when comparing pass rates across conditions so a trivial pass here isn't read as evidence of disciplined single-driver behavior.

The report names case-sensitivity of coupon codes as a stated assumption (assumption 4), and expectation 6 grades whether that assumption is stated -- which it is. But tests/pricing.test.ts never exercises a case variant of a valid code (e.g. 'save10' or 'Save10'), only unrelated garbage strings ('BOGUS', ''). The assumption is reported but left unverified by the test suite; a hidden test on case handling would let the eval check the assumption itself rather than just its disclosure.

eval_feedback.overall: The objective checks are well-grounded and each was independently confirmed against the transcript, diff, and final workspace files rather than taken on faith (tests_pass, typecheck_pass, flat5_has_test, hidden_acceptance_all_pass, and the failing test_edited_before_pricing all checked out). The one structural weak point is single_tdd_driver's vacuous truth whenever skills_invoked is empty; consider scoping it to skill-bearing conditions or reporting N/A instead of pass in that case.
